comparison: Both evaluate TEL-patch identification and genetic characterization (C3, C22-C24, C28). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with converging data from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers also find work SUPPORTED, describing it as 'thorough and thoughtful' with 'elegant genetic and biochemical approaches.' High agreement, though peer review includes C27 which OpenEval groups separately.

Both address epistasis analysis (C25, C26, C76). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriately designed controls. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, requesting additional documentation of senescent phenotype and telomere length analysis at later generations, indicating incomplete evidence. Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

Both evaluate Co-IP data on TEL-patch mutations and protein interactions (C30-C34). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong evidence for direct Tpz1-Trt1 interaction. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, requesting normalization of quantification to compensate for mutant effects on protein stability and IP efficiency. Disagreement on data interpretation rigor.
Both address ChIP data showing reduced telomerase localization (C35). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Figure 3A data. Peer reviewers also SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate fusion rescue experiments (C36-C38). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, describing it as a well-designed rescue experiment. Peer reviewers also SUPPORTED with no concerns raised. Strong agreement.

Both address mutational analysis of Ccq1-Est1 binding sites (C40-C43). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive evidence including double mutant data. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, requesting re-run with proper normalization and qualification of complete loss of interaction claims due to technical limitations. Disagreement on interpretation of binding data.

OpenEval R6 includes competitive binding assays (C44-C46) as part of two-binding-site model evidence, finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R7 specifically questions the ternary complex existence, marking it UNCERTAIN and requesting direct demonstration via super-shift EMSA or other methods. Disagreement on sufficiency of indirect evidence for ternary complex.

Both evaluate cell cycle Co-IP data linking Ccq1 phosphorylation to Tpz1-Trt1 interaction (C48-C50). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Figure 6 data. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting contradictions with other data in the paper and published work, questioning whether only a minor fraction of complexes interact. Significant disagreement on internal consistency.

Both evaluate the overall model synthesis (C4, C51-C54). OpenEval finds model SUPPORTED and well-supported by experimental findings. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about nomenclature ('transition state'), contradictions with cell cycle data, and lack of experimental support for claims about spatial information and positioning at 3' end. Major disagreement on model validity and presentation.

Both address speculative claims about preferential elongation of short telomeres (C59-C61). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN, noting it's plausible but requires validation. Peer reviewers also mark UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating work doesn't address spatial information or length-dependent elongation experimentally, appropriate for Discussion but not primary conclusions. Agreement on speculative nature.

Both address speculation about conservation to human TIN2 (C75). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN, noting it's reasonable hypothesis lacking direct support. Peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED, accepting comparative speculations as appropriate. Mild disagreement, though both recognize speculative nature.
